group.passage: For a long time, a doctor who wanted to hear what was happening inside a patient's chest usually pressed an ear against it. This often made both the doctor and the patient uncomfortable. In 1816, a French doctor named René Laennec found a better way with nothing more than a sheet of paper. That year, Laennec took a job as a doctor at the Necker Hospital in Paris. One day, a young woman with signs of heart disease came to see him. Because of her age and sex, he felt that putting his ear on her chest would not be proper. Then he remembered a simple fact about sound: when someone scratches one end of a long piece of wood with a pin, a person listening at the other end can hear it clearly. Laennec rolled a sheet of paper into a tight tube and placed one end on the woman's chest. With his ear at the other end, he heard her heartbeat far more clearly than he ever had with his ear alone. Laennec, who played the flute and carved wooden instruments in his free time, went on to make a better tool. It was a hollow wooden tube about 25 centimeters long, built in separate parts. The tube could be taken apart, so it was easy to carry. He named it the “stethoscope,” from two Greek words meaning “chest” and “to explore.” In 1819, he described the sounds of the heart and lungs in a book. At first, some doctors did not trust the new tool. Before long, however, doctors from all over Europe were traveling to Paris to learn Laennec's method. Sadly, Laennec himself became ill with tuberculosis, a disease that most often attacks the lungs. In 1824, his nephew listened to his chest with a stethoscope and found the disease. Laennec died two years later, at the age of 45. His simple idea changed the way doctors examined their patients.

evidence: Then he remembered a simple fact about sound: when someone scratches one end of a long piece of wood with a pin, a person listening at the other end can hear it clearly.

option_notes_zh.A: 文中沒有提到其他醫生給他建議，他是自己想起一個聲學事實。

2.strategy_zh: 找到雷奈克捲紙筒之前的那一句（Then he remembered…），看他想起了什麼。其他兩個在文中出現過的事件，要注意年份都在 1816 年之後。

translation_zh.text:
很長一段時間，醫生如果想聽病人胸腔裡的動靜，通常是把耳朵貼在病人胸口上。這常常讓醫生和病人都覺得不自在。1816 年，一位名叫雷奈克的法國醫生只靠一張紙，就找到了更好的方法。
那一年，雷奈克到巴黎的內克醫院擔任醫師。有一天，一位出現心臟病徵狀的年輕女子來看病。因為她的年齡和性別，雷奈克覺得把耳朵貼在她胸口並不恰當。這時他想起一個關於聲音的簡單事實：有人用針刮長木頭的一端時，在另一端聽的人能聽得很清楚。雷奈克把一張紙緊緊捲成筒，一端放在那名女子的胸口。他把耳朵貼在另一端，聽到的心跳聲比他以往直接用耳朵聽時清楚得多。
雷奈克平時會吹長笛，也會雕刻木製樂器，後來他做出了更好的工具。那是一根約 25 公分長的中空木管，分成幾段製作。這支木管可以拆開，所以很方便攜帶。他把它命名為「聽診器」（stethoscope），取自兩個希臘字，意思是「胸部」和「探查」。1819 年，他把心臟和肺部的聲音寫成了一本書。
起初，有些醫生並不信任這個新工具。不過沒過多久，歐洲各地的醫生都前往巴黎學習雷奈克的方法。令人難過的是，雷奈克自己得了肺結核，這是一種最常侵襲肺部的疾病。1824 年，他的姪子用聽診器聽他的胸腔，發現了這個病。兩年後雷奈克去世，享年 45 歲。他這個簡單的點子，改變了醫生檢查病人的方式。
